answer: Require each identity to burn real compute before it can transact: solving a fresh proof-of-work puzzle per identity, like tending a grove where every tree must be grown, not copied. A trellis of rate limits then caps how many puzzles one machine can solve per day, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand puzzles worth of electricity and hardware time. Each fake is a vertex that must pay its own way in, and the cost scales linearly with the size of the attack, pricing out cheap sybil swarms while honest agents pay once.
